findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. This is the page's strongest part.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The title and heading lead with firstmate, a project a newcomer at the Athena site has likely never heard of. The page's main subject is not Athena, and the reader only learns that from the third lede paragraph.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: Athena's main selling points, a second model checking the work and cost tracking, are stated but never shown. The whole page shows a different ability (studying a project), so the newcomer sees no example of a traced commit, a verdict or a cost.
findings.source: Header lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: The next step is concrete and linked from the top: prerequisites, clone, install and a first command. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Section "Next steps": "git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link is aimed at the project owner, yet it sits in the header that every newcomer reads first. "Your decision" misleads a visitor who owns nothing here.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Most of the page is a dense state-machine reading of firstmate's scripts. A newcomer to Athena gains little from it beyond seeing that every sentence carries a claim id.
findings.source: Sections "Transitions" and "Counters", e.g. "the spawn is deferred with exit 75", "guarded fast-forward", "pending-close record"

findings.text: Some terms are undefined or defined in circles. "Wake", "endpoint", "durable record", "merge authority" and "captain-held inventory" have no glossary entries, and "harness" is used before its glossary definition.
findings.source: t8 card: "A ship or scout keeps its recorded harness and needs a note; a secondmate re-reads its pin"; Glossary "stale wake": "A wake after which the agent inspects a worker"

findings.text: Definitions and facts repeat many times; the rule that a local-only ship or scout keeps its place until cleanup appears in at least five sections. This makes an already long page longer.
findings.source: "Words used first" vs Glossary entry "in scope": both read "The words firstmate's instructions use for the work that yolo lets firstmate merge itself..."

findings.text: Notes about Athena's internal process and repository layout are exposed to the reader. They may confuse a newcomer about whether the study can be trusted, and they do not help them.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths"; About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"

findings.text: The prerequisites imply that Athena needs Claude Code, but the page never says whether an account, API key or paid plan is required. A newcomer cannot tell what trying it will cost.
findings.source: Next steps: "have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm (to install Claude Code)"
